structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, no amphibian species (frog, toad, newt or caecilian) is native to any truly oceanic island, defined as one that arose from the sea floor and was never joined to a continent. Amphibians introduced to those islands do establish populations.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Take a pre-specified list of at least 15 oceanic islands or archipelagos: Hawaii, Galápagos, Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cape Verde, St Helena, Ascension, Tristan da Cunha, Mauritius, Réunion, Rodrigues, Bermuda, Kerguelen, Easter Island, Society Islands, Marquesas, Cook Islands and Tonga. The claim passes if the count of native amphibian species on them is 0 (strictly true, as Darwin put it). It must also hold that introduced, established amphibians are recorded on at least 40% of the listed islands (the 'introduced frogs thrive' clause).
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if at least 1 amphibian species is recorded as native or endemic on any listed oceanic island, and that record survives a check against the geological literature that the island was never connected to a continent. It also fails if introduced amphibians are established on fewer than 15% of the listed islands.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Batrachians' are modern Anura (frogs and toads) and Caudata (newts and salamanders). Caecilians (Gymnophiona) are also tested, because they are amphibians that Darwin did not mention. 'Oceanic island' follows the modern geological meaning: volcanic or atoll islands never connected to a continent. Continental fragments such as New Zealand, the Seychelles granitic islands, New Caledonia, Madagascar, Fiji, the Solomon Islands and the Falklands are excluded in advance. Fiji and New Caledonia are borderline cases and are excluded before any data are seen. 'Native' means an AmphibiaWeb species whose native range includes the island. 'Introduced' means species flagged as introduced in the AmphibiaWeb species accounts, cross-checked against the GBIF establishmentMeans field. The sea-water mechanism is not measured here. Only the distributional pattern and the establishment of introductions are tested.

dataset.name: AmphibiaWeb
dataset.why_it_fits: AmphibiaWeb is a global, curated database of amphibian species. Its species accounts give country and island distribution, and it offers a downloadable species list and search by location. Fields to use: scientific name, order, 'Distribution' / country and island, and the notes on introduced populations. These can be matched against the pre-specified island list to count native and introduced species. GBIF occurrence records can supplement the introduced-species check.
